newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: BRAAT BEHEER SAYS TAXES COULD CUT 96 NET.
newsitem.headline: BRAAT BEHEER SAYS TAXES COULD CUT 96 NET.

text.p: Textiles group Braat Beheer said on Friday it expected the current level of operating activity to continue into the second half of 1996, but cautioned its full-year results could be pressured by a tax claim.
"For the second half (of 1996) it is expected that - partly due to increasing consumer confidence - the current level of operational activity will continue," Braat said in a statement.
But it said that the full year result might be pressured by the still uncertain settlement of a tax dispute, investigations into which would be rounded off by the end of the year.

The company earlier reported first-half net profits of 0.92 million guilders, up from a year-earlier 0.88 million. The tax charge amounted to 70,000 guilders, compared to a gain of 0.55 million in the first half of 1995.
